articles.title: Midland Cornish rowing club competes in world championships
articles.summary: The Midland Cornish crew, based in Derbyshire, will compete against more experienced coastal rowers at the world championships.
articles.content: Landlocked rowers are set to make waves at sea when they compete in the world championships for Cornish pilot gig boats. Midland Cornish rowing club, based in Derbyshire, is no stranger to competition, but its crews face a unique challenge - being from an inland region with little experience of coastal rowing. The club's teams have been surprising their opponents at local events, including the Gig Racing County Championships in Plymouth, where they represented Derbyshire. Their presence often catches people off guard, with some opponents taken aback by the sight of landlocked rowers competing against them. As one of the team members, Katie Baines, noted: "They're always quite shocked." The Midland Cornish crew is gearing up for the world championships in the Isles of Scilly from April 30 to May 2, an event that draws around 2,000 rowers. The Midland Cornish crew is a rare breed in the world of traditional rowing. While over 90 clubs and more than 8,000 active gig rowers call the South West of England home, this team trains on a reservoir far from the nearest stretch of open sea. Located more than 60 miles inland, their unique situation allows them to stand out among their peers. Founded by Chris Baker, who moved from Cornwall to Derbyshire 35 years ago but only got back into rowing in the past decade, Midland Cornish has around 30 regulars on its team. Despite being a long way from the sea, the crew's performance is not lacking in spirit or competitiveness. According to Baker, his rowers are well aware of their challenge and do not take it lightly, as evidenced by their determined approach to training. "I don't think we embarrass ourselves when we turn up," Baker said confidently. The Derbyshire team's coach has a unique advantage in his experience and expertise. Martin Pezzack, a former multiple world champion from Cornwall, brings a wealth of knowledge to the table. Coaching teams that rarely get to experience the sea is particularly rewarding for him. articles.title: SpaceX Booster Rocket Explodes in Gulf of Mexico During Starship Test Flight
articles.summary: The incident occurred during a test flight of SpaceX's Starship program, which aims to demonstrate reusable booster rockets.
articles.content: SpaceX's ambitious Starship program suffered a setback on Friday when its booster rocket exploded in the Gulf of Mexico after being diverted from its original landing site. The incident prevented the company from achieving an unprecedented double catch, where both the spacecraft and the booster would be recovered at the launch pad. The mishap occurred during the test flight of the Starship, which was designed to demonstrate its ability to return to Earth from orbit using a reusable booster rocket. Despite the loss of the booster, the spacecraft continued on its journey, with plans for it to steer towards the launch pad on Saturday, pending further developments. This daring maneuver is part of SpaceX's efforts to reduce costs and increase launch frequencies by reusing as much of the rocket as possible. The goal is to achieve a level of efficiency that would enable the construction of moon bases and manned missions to Mars, according to Elon Musk's vision for the company. The original plan was to retrieve both the spacecraft and the booster using mechanical arms attached to the launch tower, a feat that has never been accomplished before anywhere in the world. With the loss of the booster, SpaceX will have to reassess its strategy for achieving this ambitious goal, which relies on the rapid recycling of rocket components. The Starship spacecraft successfully reached orbit on its maiden voyage, but a dramatic turn of events unfolded when SpaceX attempted to catch the booster in mid-air. Instead, it exploded just as it was about to be retrieved, forcing the company to reassess its strategy for achieving rapid recycling of rocket components. The loss of the booster is particularly significant because Starship had been tasked with dropping off 26 advanced Starlink satellites shortly after reaching orbit. These satellites will now have to rely on other means to continue their mission, which involves completing 15 laps around the world at an altitude of approximately 170 miles. Despite having successfully caught three boosters in previous attempts, SpaceX's latest attempt was a major setback for the company. In fact, this was the first time they had attempted to catch the upgraded version of the booster, which measures 236 feet and is intended for use on moon and Mars expeditions. The explosion also raises questions about the safety protocols in place at Starbase, where SpaceX has been testing its reusable rocket technology. According to launch commentator Kate Tice, the incident was not unexpected given the rigorous safety checks that are always conducted before a launch. This latest development will likely have significant implications for SpaceX's plans to reuse rocket components on a large scale. With the production model for moon and Mars expeditions now in question, the company will need to reassess its strategy for achieving rapid recycling of rocket components. SpaceX is gearing up for a busy launch schedule as it prepares to start sending Starships into orbit from Florida within the next few months and from Louisiana in a couple of years. The company's plans call for scaling up its infrastructure and achieving full rocket reusability to support an unprecedented pace of launches. The key to making this vision a reality is the ability to recover both stages of the rocket, which will be made possible by the Starship's advanced technology. According to SpaceX's Kiko Dontchev, vice president of launch, "how you go from zero launches to 10 to 100 to 1,000 to 10,000 to 100,000" is through this combination of infrastructure and full reusability. Meanwhile, the company will continue to rely on its smaller Falcon rockets for some missions. These will include carrying astronauts to the International Space Station for NASA and launching Starlink satellites from California. For now, Satellites will still hitch a ride on Falcons, but Musk envisions a future where Starships take over this role as well. Falcon rockets are not yet fully reusable, with the second stage being discarded after each flight. This is not the case for Starship, which Dontchev says will allow both stages to be caught and recovered. This capability is crucial for SpaceX's plans to use Starships for NASA's Artemis program, which aims to land astronauts on the moon. The stakes are high for SpaceX, as it has secured billions of dollars from NASA to develop the technology needed to land humans on the lunar surface using Starship. The company will face stiff competition from Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos' private space venture, which is also vying for a spot in the Artemis program. The Artemis III mission is set to take place next summer, where astronauts will test their skills by docking a capsule with two spacecraft in orbit around Earth: Blue Moon and Starship. This exercise will lay the groundwork for an ambitious goal - landing on the moon as early as 2028. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has expressed enthusiasm for integrating Starlink capabilities into Artemis III, which will provide valuable experience for future lunar missions. articles.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
articles.summary: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

articles.title: Protests Erupt Across Germany and Europe Over Young People's Future Prospects
articles.summary: Youth researcher Simon Schnetzer believes that young people today face significant challenges, but it's also valid to ask whether previous generations faced similar issues.
articles.content: Protests have erupted across Germany and Europe as young people express concerns about their future prospects. These demonstrations are prompting a debate: do members of Gen Z face more significant challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s? Youth researcher Simon Schnetzer has been studying this question, and he believes it's valid to ask whether things were just as tough for previous generations. However, young people today see their own struggles as a pressing issue that demands support now. According to Schnetzer, who authored the Youth in Germany study, one key concern raised by recent protests is: have we provided young people with the conditions necessary to live and work confidently here? His response is straightforward: no, we haven't. The projected decline in contributors to support retirees is stark, with numbers expected to drop significantly by 2045. The pension system will then rely on just 1.73 contributors per retiree, a ratio that highlights the strain on the financial burden of supporting an aging population. To mitigate this trend and maintain stable contribution rates, the government already provides substantial subsidies to the pension system. These annual injections amount to approximately €118 billion, which accounts for roughly 25% of the federal budget. This significant allocation underscores the importance of addressing the underlying issues driving the decline in contributors. The strain on the pension system is evident in the rising numbers of retirees relying on basic income support from the government. Between 2003 and 2024, this figure has increased from 257,000 to 738,000, indicating that many retirees are struggling to make ends meet. The financial burden on low-income households is significant, particularly when it comes to housing costs. Data from Germany's Federal Statistical Office reveals that these households spend a substantial amount more of their disposable income on rent compared to high-income households. In 2025, an alarming 11% of the population will struggle with housing costs exceeding 40% of their disposable income. The situation is even more dire for those at risk of poverty, where 35% of their income goes towards housing expenses. This stark reality highlights the pressing need for affordable housing solutions. A report by real estate platform Jacasa suggests that a potential solution lies in the transfer of properties from Baby Boomers to younger generations. With approximately 4.8 million owner-occupied houses and apartments currently owned by this demographic, there is a significant pool of properties expected to change hands in the coming years. As these properties are sold or passed down through inheritance, it could lead to an oversupply in certain regions, resulting in lower property prices according to Jacasa's projections. This development may provide much-needed relief for younger generations struggling with housing costs. Public spending on education has increased significantly since 2011, rising from approximately €4,000 to around €8,000 per person annually. Despite this increase, Germany ranks only mid-table internationally in terms of public education spending as a percentage of GDP. The additional funding allocated to education cannot solely address the issue of teacher shortages in Germany. Estimates suggest that by 2035, the country will be short approximately 27,000 teachers due to a combination of factors including the retirement of Baby Boomers and declining birth rates. This has resulted in a scarcity of young teachers entering the profession. The Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs has highlighted this pressing concern, emphasizing that teacher shortages are a far-reaching problem that cannot be easily resolved by increased funding alone. The consequences of climate change are a stark reminder of the challenges facing future generations. According to the United Nations, global warming is on track to reach 2.6°C above pre-industrial levels by the end of the century if current policies remain in place. Heat waves, in particular, will become more frequent and severe for children growing up today. A study published by Vrije University in Brussels projected that six-year-olds could experience heat waves two to seven times as often as their Boomer counterparts did over a lifetime. Youth researcher Schnetzer emphasizes that Baby Boomers and Gen Z are facing similar challenges, which necessitates a joint approach to address their shared concerns. By uniting both generations in protests, they can collectively push for change and create prospects for prosperity. Schnetzer advocates for a constructive process following the protests, where goals and measures are defined to ensure everyone's support, even if it means making sacrifices. He believes that this collaborative effort is just the beginning of a necessary shift towards a more sustainable future. articles.summary: The matchup could have significant implications for LSU's College Football Playoff chances, while Texas seeks to extend its winning streak against ranked opponents.
articles.content: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin has a personal stake in Saturday's matchup against No. 6 Texas, a game that could have significant implications for his team's College Football Playoff chances. The Tigers are trying to avoid consecutive home losses under Kiffin's leadership, a feat they last accomplished in 1994. The stakes are high for both teams, with the loser potentially being eliminated from playoff contention. LSU is looking to bounce back from its first home loss since Kiffin took over, while Texas seeks to extend its winning streak against ranked opponents to seven games. A top-two team has lost in five consecutive weeks, a feat that ties 2007 for the longest such stretch in AP Top 25 history. This week's matchups feature several teams with crucial games on their schedules, including No. 1 Georgia and No. 2 Utah. No. 1 Georgia is hosting No. 22 Missouri, which has yet to beat an AP No. 1 team in its 18 attempts. The Bulldogs have a strong home record against ranked opponents, but the Tigers will be looking to upset their hosts. The same weekend, No. 2 Utah visits No. 23 Arizona as a slight favorite. The Utes' starting quarterback has a good track record against the Wildcats, having won both of his previous meetings with them. Indiana's Josh Hoover is back on the field after dealing with an injury, but the Hoosiers will be without their leading rusher Turbo Richard in their matchup against No. 18 USC. In another notable game, No. 12 Texas Tech faces off against No. 25 Oklahoma State, a contest that has significant implications for both teams' conference standings. The Southeastern Conference (SEC) championship picture is still unclear, but Georgia can secure its spot in the final with a win on Saturday and some help from other teams in the league. Indiana's recent performances have shown that they tend to be closely contested games. Five of their six Big Ten matchups so far this season have been decided by a touchdown or less. The Hoosiers' physicality on both lines of scrimmage has proven to be a key factor in their success, but it remains to be seen if they can overcome the more experienced USC team and its veteran quarterback Jayden Maiava. The Georgia Bulldogs have shown impressive consistency this season, but they'll be facing a Missouri team that's capable of causing an upset if given the opportunity. A big win over Ole Miss has left some wondering if the Bulldogs will let their guard down against the Tigers, who are looking to make a statement in this matchup. While Missouri has been competitive in several games, it still remains to be seen whether they have what it takes to beat a top-ranked team like Georgia. Kirby Smart is known for his strategic approach, and it's hard to imagine him letting his team get complacent. The Bulldogs' dominance on the field has been evident in their recent wins, but Missouri could potentially exploit any weaknesses if Georgia becomes overconfident. A loss would be a significant setback for the Tigers, who are still trying to find their footing this season. If they can't pull off an upset, they'll need to regroup and reassess their chances of making a strong finish. Georgia's ability to maintain its momentum will be crucial in this matchup, as Missouri looks to capitalize on any errors or lapses in focus by the Bulldogs. articles.title: Pope Leo XIV Visit Triggers Measles Concerns in South America
articles.summary: Millions of Catholics have gathered to see Pope Leo XIV, but health authorities are worried about the spread of measles due to mass gatherings.
articles.content: Millions of Catholics have gathered in South America to catch a glimpse of Pope Leo XIV, but health authorities are more concerned about another visitor: measles. The highly contagious virus has been spreading rapidly in the region this year, and mass gatherings like these pose a significant risk. Cases of measles have already surged in South America, creating an opportunity for the virus to spread further among the large crowds. Health officials have been preparing for potential problems by mounting vaccination campaigns and increasing surveillance efforts to limit the spread of the disease. In Uruguay, thousands of people attended a prayer vigil and Mass celebrated by Pope Leo XIV, prompting health authorities to take extra precautions. The country has implemented intensified surveillance monitoring until November 29, three weeks after the Pope's departure. Uruguay has also been working to boost its vaccination rate, which is now among the highest in the region. The director of epidemiology at Uruguay's health ministry, Nataly Rodriguez, emphasizes the importance of keeping vaccination schedules up to date as a preventive strategy against measles outbreaks. By prioritizing vaccinations and surveillance efforts, health officials hope to contain the spread of the virus and protect vulnerable populations. The upcoming visit by Pope Leo to South America has raised concerns about public health risks, particularly regarding measles outbreaks in the region. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has assessed the situation as "very high due to a significant increase in cases between January and October this year compared to the same period last year. According to Daniel Salas Peraza, head of immunization at PAHO, the rise in measles cases is having a devastating impact on children. We're seeing children not going to school, children being hospitalized, he said, highlighting the complexity of the situation. The high number of infections is particularly alarming given the region's large Catholic population. Measles spreads rapidly through the air when an infected person breathes, sneezes or coughs, making it a highly contagious disease. What's more, individuals can be contagious even before they show symptoms, which can include a high fever, runny nose, cough and rash. The virus primarily affects children, although it is rarely fatal. The measles vaccine is extremely effective in preventing the spread of the disease. However, to achieve herd immunity and protect vulnerable populations such as infants who cannot receive the vaccine until their first birthday, at least 95% of a community must be fully vaccinated with two doses. This requirement underscores the importance of widespread vaccination efforts. Given the high public health risk associated with the upcoming mass gatherings in South America, PAHO's assessment is a stark reminder of the need for urgent action to contain measles outbreaks and protect vulnerable populations. Measles cases have surged significantly across South America in recent months, prompting concerns about public health. According to data from the World Health Organization, Peru has made notable strides in vaccination efforts, achieving 90% coverage for one dose and 82% for two doses. However, neighboring countries such as Argentina trail behind, with only 84% of children receiving their first dose and a mere 55% fully vaccinated against measles. This disparity highlights the region's uneven progress in combating the highly contagious disease. The number of confirmed cases has skyrocketed to nearly five times that recorded during the same period last year, with 57,666 reported across 17 countries and territories in the Americas between January and October. Sadly, at least 81 lives have been lost due to measles this year alone. Peru is among the hardest-hit nations, accounting for nearly 3,000 of the region's cases, placing it fourth on the list after Guatemala, Mexico, and the United States. The country's five cities scheduled to host the Pope's visit next month are also hotspots for measles transmission, with a total of 170 cases identified so far this year. To mitigate the spread of the disease ahead of the high-profile visit, PAHO has been working closely with local authorities in Peru to boost vaccination efforts. This includes initiatives targeting adolescents and strengthening vaccine storage and delivery capacity in areas along the border with Brazil. With millions expected at the pope's visit to Argentina, concerns over low vaccination rates are escalating. The country has been struggling to keep up with immunization efforts, particularly after a measles outbreak in April 2025 resulted in the first death from the disease in two decades. This has left many worried that the situation is dire and may worsen with the large crowds anticipated for the pope's visit. Argentina President Javier Milei's decision to slash the country's healthcare budget has only added to the problem, as agencies responsible for planning, financing, and tracking immunization campaigns have been severely impacted. The cuts come at a critical time when efforts are needed to boost vaccination rates in areas with low immunity levels. Despite these challenges, Marcela Lopez Yunes, a doctor and pediatric infectious disease specialist, emphasizes that public communication is key to encouraging people to get vaccinated. We need to do more to give diseases such as measles the attention they deserve," she stressed. Meanwhile, Argentina's health ministry has maintained that while it purchases and distributes vaccines nationwide, provinces are responsible for administering them to their populations. The ministry also confirmed that a public service announcement is currently airing to highlight the importance of vaccination in general. As Pope Francis visits South America, concerns about measles outbreaks are growing due to large crowds and low vaccination rates in several countries. The pontiff's arrival in Argentina on Sunday coincided with criticism of austerity measures by opposition leader Javier Milei, who emphasized the need for leaders to prioritize people over economic interests. Meanwhile, vaccination efforts continue amidst a surge in measles cases, prompting public health officials to stress the importance of immunization. articles.title: Huang Yi-hao involved in deliberate car attack
articles.summary: Taiwanese comedian Huang Yi-hao was attacked by five individuals who caused his vehicle to collide with another car.
articles.content: A comedian in Taiwan was involved in a car accident that turned out to be a deliberate attack on his life. The incident occurred in September when Huang Yi-hao's vehicle collided with another car, but what followed was unusual - the men involved were excessively courteous and even offered to cover the medical expenses and damage. However, further investigation by Taiwanese police revealed that this was no ordinary accident. In fact, it was a case of attempted assault on Huang, who had become a target for his criticisms of China's government. The authorities have since charged five individuals in connection with the incident. The alleged attack on Huang is part of a growing trend where Chinese operatives are being sent to Taiwan to harass or harm individuals who are seen as critical of Beijing. According to Chiu Shao-Chou, commissioner of Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau, these incidents have become increasingly severe over time. Chiu noted that the methods used by these operatives have evolved from verbal harassment and property damage to more serious forms of intimidation, such as causing fake car accidents. Taiwanese authorities are concerned about this trend and are taking steps to address it. Taiwanese officials have long been wary of Chinese infiltration attempts on the island, which is a self-ruled democracy claimed by Beijing. The government has identified various methods used by China to exert influence over Taiwan, including spy plots, disinformation schemes, and cultural exchanges that promote Communist Party ideology. Taiwanese authorities are investigating a series of violent attacks on critics of China, raising concerns about transnational repression. The tactics used by China to harass or harm dissidents abroad have been exposed in recent years, including secret police stations set up in foreign countries to surveil Chinese nationals who speak out against the government. In 2023, law enforcement officials in New York made arrests related to such a station. Prosecutors claim that five men were hired to seriously injure comedian Lee Huang, allegedly for a payment of about 450,000 New Taiwan dollars ($13,900) from someone using the alias "K from China. The incident may be linked to Huang's performance last year, in which he compared Chinese President Xi Jinping to Winnie the Pooh. The attack has had an unexpected consequence: Lee Huang's solo shows have sold out since the incident, with his fans rallying around him. Huang believes that his criticism of Xi is the reason behind the violent attempt on his life and also thinks that other comedians who collaborated with him may face repercussions in China and Taiwan. Lee Huang has no intention of taking his performances to China, but he did express surprise at the aggressive response from Beijing following his criticism of President Xi. The Communist Party is very childish, he said in a statement, questioning why China would react so strongly to a comedian's jokes. Taiwanese prosecutors have revealed details of a plot by Hong Kong gangsters to assault Japanese political commentator Akio Yaita, describing it as another example of transnational repression. The alleged attack was planned and paid for by a fellow gangster, with five triad members entering Taiwan in early July to scope out the area around the hotel where Yaita was scheduled to give a speech. Two of them eventually withdrew from the mission, leaving only two men who were tasked with carrying out the assault. One of these men was offered 100,000 Hong Kong dollars to physically harm Yaita, and he ultimately punched the commentator in the face. He has since been arrested, while his accomplice fled Taiwan after acting as a lookout during the attack. The incident has left many concerned about the implications for freedom of speech in Taiwan. Yaita himself believes that the assault was directly linked to his criticisms of China's government policies, and he remains unapologetic about speaking out against them. Yaita's comments have sparked concerns among experts who believe that anyone in Taiwan who dares to criticize Xi Jinping and the Chinese Communist Party could be a potential target. The arrest of a woman in Los Angeles for allegedly conducting surveillance on Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te's son has raised concerns about the involvement of the Chinese government in transnational repression. Taiwanese authorities are coordinating closely with their US counterparts to address similar cases that involve Taiwanese nationals overseas, highlighting the global reach of Beijing's alleged tactics against its critics. The threat is not limited to Taiwan alone, according to police officials who acknowledge a coordinated effort by various agencies to counter this emerging trend. Chiu, the police commissioner, emphasized the gravity of these incidents, stating that they pose a significant threat to national security and require immediate investigation. He also noted that police treat such cases as national-level threats, necessitating coordination with immigration authorities, the coast guard, and other government agencies. The Taiwan Affairs Office has strongly denied any involvement in the violent attack on Huang, a Taiwanese artist who was targeted for his criticism of China's government. The office claimed that accusations of transnational repression were baseless and part of a smear campaign by Taiwan's ruling Democratic Progressive Party. In response to the allegations, the party had introduced legislation aimed at suppressing political dissidents and limiting cross-strait exchanges, sparking concerns over freedom of speech in Taiwan. For Huang, however, the attack sent a chilling message that criticizing China comes with a price. They want to silence anyone who dares to speak out against them," he said, underscoring the fear that his actions had provoked a reprisal from Beijing. articles.title: Measles Cases Erupt in US After Over 25 Years Without Continuous Spread
articles.summary: A series of major measles outbreaks has prompted the Pan American Health Organization to reassess the country's elimination status.
articles.content: Measles cases have started appearing in the United States after more than 25 years without continuous domestic spread of the disease. The country was officially declared measles-free in 2000, but occasional outbreaks still occurred due to travelers bringing the virus into the country. These isolated incidents did not lead to ongoing transmission of the disease within the US population. However, a recent series of major measles outbreaks has changed this status, prompting the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) to reassess the country's elimination status. The PAHO, which is the regional office of the World Health Organization for the Americas, has now determined that the US should be considered non-eliminated. This decision comes after a significant increase in measles cases, with nearly 2,300 reported nationwide in 2025 and over 5,412 confirmed so far this year. A leading health expert has warned that the resurgence of measles could be the point of no return, as outbreaks become increasingly difficult to control. The resurgence of measles in the US is a stark reminder that maintaining high vaccination rates is crucial to preventing large outbreaks. For measles, achieving herd immunity requires at least 95% of the population to be immune through either vaccination or past infection, as its virus spreads rapidly and easily from person to person. In recent years, however, national measles vaccination rates have been steadily declining, with only 10 states reporting rates above the critical threshold among kindergarteners for the 2025-2026 school year. Experts point to a combination of factors contributing to this trend, including decreasing funding and personnel for public health initiatives as well as wavering confidence in vaccines and scientific expertise among the general population. The appointment of an individual with a history of questioning vaccine safety and efficacy has likely exacerbated these issues by creating confusion around established vaccine guidance. According to health authorities, a significant number of measles cases in the United States result in death, with approximately 1 to 3 out of every 1,000 cases being fatal. The high number of reported deaths in Pennsylvania is particularly concerning, as it suggests that the state's true case rate may be higher than what has been captured by data. With over 1,500 measles cases recorded in the state, this discrepancy raises questions about the accuracy of the reported numbers. Measles can have severe long-term health consequences for survivors, including brain damage and immune amnesia. In individuals who contract the virus, their immune system's "memory" is essentially wiped clean, leaving them vulnerable to other infections. The recent surge in measles cases in the United States serves as a stark reminder of the importance of vaccination and immunity. articles.title: Nationwide air traffic control outage causes thousands of flight cancellations
articles.summary: The disruption resulted in nearly 7,500 flight cancellations, causing widespread travel chaos as airlines pointed to the uncontrollable nature of the ATC outage.
articles.content: A nationwide air traffic control outage has left thousands of passengers stranded across the US. The disruption resulted in nearly 7,500 flight cancellations, causing widespread travel chaos. Air travelers were left to navigate the crisis on their own as airlines pointed to the uncontrollable nature of the ATC outage. According to the Department of Transportation, disruptions caused by uncontrollable factors do not require airlines to provide freebies such as hotel stays or food vouchers. The situation has been exacerbated by the sheer number of cancellations, making it nearly impossible for passengers to get a seat on a flight this weekend. Travelers are now forced to fend for themselves, seeking out alternative arrangements at their own expense. The Department of Transportation's customer service dashboard provides information on passenger compensation for flights disrupted by controllable factors, such as maintenance or crew scheduling, but it does not apply to the current situation. Airlines may offer goodwill vouchers to help out affected customers, but it's essential to understand that these are not guaranteed. When booking travel arrangements such as hotels or rental cars, passengers may be able to claim eligible expenses from their credit card issuer. Airline passengers have certain rights in the US, as outlined by the Department of Transportation. However, there is no law requiring carriers to compensate for disruptions caused by uncontrollable events like weather or air traffic control delays. If your flight is canceled, you're entitled to a full refund, including any add-ons like baggage fees or seat upgrades. This must be refunded in the original form of payment. Airlines have varying policies in place when it comes to disruptions they can control, such as cancellations or delays. The US Department of Transportation's Airline Customer Service Dashboard provides insight into what the 10 largest US airlines promise their customers in these situations, including options for rebooking flights, meal vouchers, and hotel accommodations. When a flight is delayed or canceled, many airlines allow passengers to adjust their travel plans online through their website or mobile app. This can be a more efficient way to make changes than waiting on the phone or visiting a physical customer service location. Travelers affected by flight cancellations can reach out to their airlines for assistance. The contact numbers for major carriers vary, with some providing phone support and others offering alternative methods like text messaging or online chat. Alaska Airlines can be reached at 1-800-252-7522 or via text message to 82008, while Allegiant customers can call 1-702-505-8888. American Airlines offers a similar option at 1-800-433-7300, and Avelo passengers can contact the airline at 1-346-616-9500. Delta customers have access to support through their phone number, 1-800-221-1212, while those with Frontier can try online chat or email for assistance. JetBlue is available at 1-800-538-2583 and Southwest passengers can call 1-800-435-9792. Several airlines offer meal or hotel vouchers to customers experiencing delays or cancellations that result in a wait of three hours or more, including overnight stays. Carriers offering both are listed on the DoT dashboard as part of their contingency plans. If you're unsure about compensation for flight disruptions not listed on the DoT dashboard, it's always best to ask your airline directly. Airlines may offer goodwill gestures during uncontrollable disruptions like winter storms, so don't hesitate to request assistance with meals or hotel accommodations. Some credit card companies provide travel insurance that can reimburse customers for unexpected expenses such as hotels, food, and transportation when flights are disrupted. Major banks like Chase and American Express offer cards with trip protection, which means cardholders who purchased their flights using these cards may be eligible for reimbursement. If your flight has been canceled due to an FAA ground stop, it's essential to be proactive about finding alternative ways to reach your destination. Consider renting a car or taking public transportation like trains or buses as viable options. Delays and cancellations are unavoidable in such situations, but being flexible can make the experience more bearable. Once you've decided on a course of action, set a time limit for yourself to wait for a resolution. If that deadline passes without any progress, it's time to explore other ways to reach your destination, which may also be covered by travel insurance. articles.title: Bobby Pulido accepts award at Latin Grammys
articles.summary: Bobby Pulido accepted an award for best Tejano album at the Latin Grammys while confirming his retirement from music.
articles.content: Bobby Pulido, a Democrat who recently won a competitive race to flip Texas' Republican-held 15th Congressional district, accepted an award for best Tejano album at the Latin Grammys. Onstage, he wore his signature cowboy hat as he confirmed his retirement from music but expressed gratitude for representing both the politics and music of Texas. The win marked Pulido's third time taking home this award in this category, although it was his first victory since being elected to Congress. His presence at the ceremony was a notable moment amidst several other politically charged references. Pulido told the audience that he felt immense pride in representing the Tejano music and culture of Texas. He underscored the significance of being from the Lone Star State and having the opportunity to bring its politics and music to the forefront. The Latin Grammys have a history of hosting performances that address social issues, including racism in American politics and human rights crises in Mexico. As Pulido accepted his award, it was clear that he has a deep connection to the Tejano culture and is committed to representing it on both the national stage and in Congress. The Latin Grammys ceremony was filled with powerful messages of change and representation, echoing a theme that resonated across music and politics. "We have to represent, Pulido said in his speech, emphasizing the importance of using one's voice for positive impact. The message of empowerment was palpable as artists took to the stage to accept their awards. The ceremony saw Daddy Yankee crowned Person of the Year, an honor he wore with pride draped in a flowing cape bearing the Puerto Rican flag. He used his platform to emphasize the significance of Puerto Rico's presence on the map. Silvana Estrada, a Mexican folk musician who has long advocated against femicide in her home country, underscored the critical role musicians play today. We have a super important job, she said, highlighting the responsibility that comes with using one's voice for social justice. The Latin Grammys have long been a celebration of music and culture from across the region. However, this year's ceremony saw a notable shift towards using the platform to address pressing social issues. Brazilian artist Anitta made headlines when she won the award for best pop contemporary Portuguese album, marking the first time an award in that language was given out during the televised event. Anitta used her moment in the spotlight to call for unity and recognition of Black culture in Brazil, highlighting the importance of representation and inclusivity. Her words were a powerful reminder that music can be a catalyst for change and social justice. By using her platform to speak out against erasure and promote cultural preservation, Anitta set an example for artists everywhere. As the ceremony progressed, it became clear that this year's Latin Grammys were not just about celebrating music, but also about amplifying marginalized voices. Artists like Anitta are paving the way for a new generation of musicians who are using their art to advocate for social justice and human rights. The impact of these performances extends far beyond the stage, with many fans taking to social media to express their support and solidarity with the artists speaking out on behalf of their communities. This shift towards more overtly political music is a welcome development, one that reflects the changing times and the growing demand for representation and inclusivity in all areas of society. The Latin Grammys have become more than just an award ceremony for music enthusiasts, but a platform to showcase the intersection of art and politics. According to Sayre, the event's founder, this convergence is not surprising given its purpose - to recognize the diverse musical landscape of Latin America. As political shifts swept across the Western Hemisphere this year, with right-wing movements in some countries and progressive changes in others, music has followed suit, reflecting the changing times. It doesn't split that cleanly, Sayre noted, highlighting the connection between musical and political evolution. The correlation between artistic expression and societal change is undeniable, with music often serving as a reflection of its cultural context. As Sayre aptly put it, I don't think you can ever look at music, or how we value music, as independent from a political landscape." This understanding underscores the significance of events like the Latin Grammys in today's world. articles.title: Social relationships crucial to scaling agricultural innovations
articles.summary: A recent study has highlighted the importance of social relationships in scaling agricultural innovations, which is a complex challenge that requires both technical solutions and strong social connections among actors involved.
articles.content: A recent study published in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems has shed light on a crucial aspect of climate-oriented agricultural research: the role of social relationships in scaling innovations. While partnerships and institutional collaboration are often emphasized, their connection to the scaling process remains understudied. This lack of understanding hinders efforts to ensure that agricultural advancements reach more farmers, influence policy, and drive lasting transformations. The scaling of agricultural innovations is a complex challenge that requires technical solutions as well as strong social relationships among actors involved in these processes. Trust, partnerships, and collaboration are essential for expanding the reach of agricultural research and development initiatives. However, the current state of knowledge leaves much to be desired, making it difficult to design effective monitoring and evaluation systems. The study "Social capital and scaling in climate-oriented Agricultural Research for Development" investigates how social relationships contribute to the scaling process. By examining existing literature on the topic, researchers aim to better understand the role of trust, closeness, and support among actors involved in agricultural innovation. This knowledge is crucial for strengthening the design, monitoring, and evaluation of scaling processes. The study's findings highlight the need for a more nuanced understanding of social relationships in climate-oriented agricultural research. By exploring the intersection of technical solutions and social dynamics, researchers can develop more effective strategies for scaling innovations that benefit farmers, policymakers, and communities worldwide. The analysis of 273 results reports has revealed a significant gap between reported outcomes and the documentation of social and institutional conditions that can facilitate scaling. This discrepancy suggests that researchers often overlook the importance of these factors in achieving successful scaling. A team of researchers from the International Center for Tropical Agriculture, the University of Copenhagen, and the Gates Foundation analyzed reports covering 261 projects across 12 CGIAR research programs. The reports were submitted between 2018 and 2021 under the former CGIAR Research Program on Climate Change, Agriculture and Food Security. The study has identified three key scaling pathways: scaling out, which involves expanding innovations to more people and places; scaling up, where policies and institutions are influenced by these innovations; and scaling deep, which transforms relationships, practices, and social norms. While the reports provide examples of these pathways, particularly scaling out and scaling up, they often lack a detailed explanation of how partnerships, trust, and institutional collaboration contribute to these processes. The researchers have found that the scaling deep dimension is notably underdeveloped in the analyzed documents, suggesting that this aspect is frequently overlooked in research. This omission can hinder the development of effective strategies for scaling innovations that benefit farmers, policymakers, and communities worldwide. By examining the intersection of technical solutions and social dynamics, researchers can gain a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that facilitate successful scaling. This knowledge can be used to inform the development of more effective scaling strategies that take into account the complex social relationships involved in achieving these goals. The analysis used a statistical model to identify patterns in the reports, categorizing them into four main areas: agricultural systems, climate change adaptation, climate change mitigation, and enabling environments. This exercise revealed 17 distinct topics within these categories. However, the researchers found that the reports often fail to explicitly connect collaborative relationships with scaling outcomes, leaving this potential connection implicit. By recognizing and documenting such connections, it is possible to enhance learning across projects and develop more effective strategies for scaling innovations. The study's findings highlight a gap in documentation, where social capital plays a significant role in research experiences but its relationship with scaling pathways remains unexplored. This lack of systematic documentation hinders the comparison of experiences and limits institutional learning. Examples from the study illustrate how partnerships based on trust and collaboration can facilitate different scaling pathways, such as the dissemination of drought-tolerant bean varieties to over 10,000 farmers across three countries through sustained relationships among national agricultural research organizations, seed companies, and farmer associations. The study highlights another example where collaboration between researchers and governments led to a significant outcome: incorporating agroclimatic information into nationally determined contributions under the Paris Agreement in several countries. This collaboration is exemplified by the Local Technical Agroclimatic Committees (MTA) in Colombia, which demonstrate how sustained interaction among farmers, extension agents, and local authorities can foster trust and facilitate the use of climate information. These committees illustrate a successful model that strengthens relationships between stakeholders. Governments, development organizations, and research programs can benefit from explicitly integrating social capital into their theories of change, planning, and monitoring strategies for scaling agricultural innovations. This involves identifying key actors and relationships and incorporating indicators such as trust, collaboration, network diversity, and participation. The authors also warn that networks can sometimes generate inequalities or exclude certain actors, emphasizing the need to understand these dynamics to promote responsible and inclusive scaling. Ignoring these issues could lead to unintended consequences. To better grasp the role of social capital in scaling pathways, researchers recommend explicitly recognizing and documenting its impact throughout project design, implementation, and monitoring phases. This could improve understanding of the conditions necessary for successful expansion of agricultural innovations. Researchers have highlighted the importance of social relationships in scaling up agricultural innovations, a crucial aspect that has been largely overlooked in previous studies. The study emphasizes that building strong connections among stakeholders is vital for the successful expansion of new farming techniques and technologies. By fostering trust and cooperation, farmers can share knowledge and best practices, leading to more efficient use of resources and improved crop yields. This could ultimately contribute to sustainable food systems and mitigate the impacts of climate change on agriculture. articles.title: Microsoft outage affects millions worldwide
articles.summary: A widespread Microsoft outage on November 12 left millions of people unable to send emails or access workplace tools like Teams.
articles.content: A widespread Microsoft outage on November 12 left millions of people worldwide unable to send emails, access Outlook, or use workplace tools like Teams. This led to a ripple effect that extended far beyond offices and workplaces. For many employees, the disruption was seen as an unexpected bonus - some even joked about it. "Thank you Microsoft," one user quipped, "Can you do this every Friday?" The impact of the outage, however, went well beyond the corporate world. Police departments struggled to receive online crime reports, while hospitals had to rely on alternative communication methods. In some areas, government services were temporarily suspended due to the disruption. This highlighted the degree to which essential public services have come to depend on a single private company's technology. The Microsoft outage exposed how vulnerable critical systems are when they rely on external providers. A seemingly ordinary email outage can have far-reaching consequences for public safety, healthcare, and justice. The incident served as a stark reminder of the risks associated with over-reliance on digital infrastructure. The disruption was felt across multiple jurisdictions, including California and Florida. In Los Angeles County, the Sheriff's Department reported problems with its email system, while the county district attorney's office also experienced disruptions. Law enforcement agencies in other areas, such as Colorado and St. Lucie County, were also affected by the outage. Email troubles plagued British police forces on Thursday, including Dorset, Cumbria, South Wales, Wiltshire, and Dyfed-Powys, which struggled to receive online crime reports. Some British police officers and staff were unable to access their Outlook accounts, a critical tool for their work. However, emergency phone lines remained operational, allowing the public to reach them in times of need. The disruption caused inconvenience but did not compromise safety. In Maine's judicial system, email submissions after 12:30 p.m. on Thursday may have gone unnoticed by courts. This has significant implications for those seeking protection orders, who must now rely on alternative methods to ensure their requests are received. In New York City, evictions scheduled for November 13 were put on hold due to the Microsoft outage. The city's Department of Investigation consulted with the Civil Court before making this decision, highlighting the far-reaching consequences of the disruption. Legislative work and local governments also suffered from the outage. Congressional staffers on Capitol Hill struggled to access their email and calendars, while cities such as Austin, Texas, Jacksonville, Florida, Richmond, Virginia, and Laurel, Maryland, pointed residents to alternative channels for communication. Asian governments were not immune to Microsoft's system failure. Australia's top spy agency confirmed it had been impacted by the glitch, along with its police force. Singapore's Government Technology Agency reported disruptions to government systems, but emergency services and a key identity verification system remained operational. Japan's Foreign Ministry was unable to send or receive emails due to the outage. In Canada, Unity Health Toronto declared a Code Grey alert after staff encountered difficulties sending and receiving emails. Despite this, patient care continued uninterrupted at its hospitals. The hospital network assured that all facilities stayed open. Britain's National Health Service also struggled with Microsoft's system failure. According to reports, healthcare workers faced issues accessing email, appointment information, and patient data. Some services resorted to backup systems or manual records due to the disruption. Email disruptions caused by the Microsoft outage had significant consequences for travelers in Canada and Britain. VIA Rail advised its passengers to use alternative methods to track their train journeys, such as the train tracker or text alerts, due to potential issues with receiving trip emails. In addition to rail services, airlines also experienced email problems, although flight operations were largely unaffected. IndiGo and Cathay Pacific reported difficulties with sending and receiving emails, but passengers were able to access their ticket information through other means if necessary. The scale of the outage is difficult to determine, given Microsoft's vast user base. The company revealed in January that over 450 million paid Microsoft 365 commercial seats existed, but it remains unclear how many users were impacted by the email disruption. The loss of Outlook functionality had far-reaching implications for individuals and businesses alike. Those who relied on verification codes or password-reset links via email to access other accounts may have found themselves locked out of online banking, payment systems, and more, even if those services themselves were functioning normally. The economic impact of the Microsoft outage is still being assessed, but one thing is clear: the productivity losses are substantial. A recent survey conducted by Public Opinion Strategies for Google found that 84% of government employees in the D.C. area rely on Microsoft products to get their work done. This dependence on a single provider has been a concern for years, with many experts warning about the risks of an IT monoculture. A report co-commissioned by Google and the Computer & Communications Industry Association found that Microsoft holds 85% of the U.S. government's office productivity software market. The appeal of using a single platform is undeniable, organizations can simplify their operations by having one provider for email, calendars, meetings, and document sharing. However, it appears that many governments stick with Microsoft due to inertia rather than innovation. According to Google's survey, 59% of respondents who use Microsoft at work say their employers chose the software because it was the most effective tool for their jobs, while 41% say their employers had always used Microsoft and were reluctant to change. A recent Government Accountability Office report highlights the challenges of diversifying IT systems in federal agencies. The report analyzed 24 government departments, revealing that 11 faced technical difficulties when integrating multiple cloud vendors due to interoperability issues and 10 struggled with resource constraints in building a skilled cloud workforce. Microsoft has acknowledged that a technical glitch arose from an earlier network capacity upgrade, which resurfaced after a subsequent network change. The company stated that the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or AI malfunction and apologized for the disruption it caused. This incident underscores the fragility of critical systems in the US. The absence of malicious intent is notable, as Google's warning about hackers four years ago predicted a different scenario. In reality, a routine network change at Microsoft triggered widespread disruptions, impacting courts, government offices, police departments, and hospitals, forcing them to resort to manual processes. articles.title: Hokkaido University and Kyoto University Researchers Study Electron Behavior in Alpha-Gallium Oxide
articles.summary: Researchers at Hokkaido University and Kyoto University have discovered that the effective mass of electrons in alpha-gallium oxide films is approximately 40% of a free electron's mass.
articles.content: Researchers have made a significant discovery about the behavior of electrons in alpha-gallium oxide, a material crucial for power electronic devices that convert electrical energy into various forms. These devices are essential for electric vehicles, renewable energy systems, and industrial equipment, but they often suffer from inefficiency due to heat loss during the process. The ability to withstand high voltages and efficiently transfer electricity while releasing heat effectively is key to making these devices more reliable. Alpha-gallium oxide has shown promise in this regard, as it can handle strong electric fields. However, scientists have yet to fully comprehend how easily electrons move through it or how effectively it dissipates heat, both critical factors for creating dependable electronic devices. To gain a deeper understanding of these properties, researchers at Hokkaido University and Kyoto University created thin films of alpha-gallium oxide using mist chemical vapor deposition. They introduced small amounts of germanium into the material to facilitate electron movement. The addition of germanium allowed the team to manipulate the concentration of electrons in the material by varying the amount added. This enabled them to study how changes in electron density affected the flow of electricity and heat through the films, providing valuable insights for improving device performance. The researchers took a closer look at the electrical properties of alpha-gallium oxide films by measuring electron concentration and thermopower, which is a measure of the voltage generated per unit temperature difference across a material. These measurements revealed an unexpected trend - the effective mass of electrons in these films was approximately 40% of a free electron's mass. This value is higher than the theoretically predicted value of 25%, suggesting that electrons behave differently than expected within alpha-gallium oxide. The study also examined how efficiently heat travels through these films, determining their thermal conductivity to be around 19 watts per meter-kelvin. Notably, this thermal conductivity remained relatively stable even when germanium concentration was increased. Further analysis of the results indicates that incorporating germanium can facilitate electron movement without significantly impacting heat transfer through the material. This finding offers a valuable insight for future device development. The study's findings suggest that alpha-gallium oxide's electrical properties are influenced by the behavior of its electrons, which deviate from theoretical expectations. This unexpected electron behavior may be responsible for the slower-than-predicted flow of electrical current in alpha-gallium oxide devices, a crucial consideration for their development. The research team's experimental approach and thorough analysis provide valuable insights into the material's properties and potential applications. As a result, this study offers a significant contribution to the field of materials science. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-heavier-electron-behavior-slower-electrical.html
